assessment:
Five tutors, split by where the card lands. Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn and Enlightened Tutor put it on top of your library; all three are instants, so the card is your next draw if you cast them at the end step before your turn, or the first card of Gishath's reveal if you cast them in combat before damage. Huatli, Poet of Unity puts a basic land in your hand when she enters, and her saga's third chapter puts any Dinosaur card in your hand two turns after you flip her. Natural Order is the one that puts a body straight onto the battlefield: sacrifice a green creature, and a green creature card from the library arrives at sorcery speed.

Most wishes answer the climb. Gishath is on the battlefield by turn six in 40.5% of 10,000 goldfish games, mean cast turn 6.706, and not by turn ten in 1,396. Knight of the Stampede and Otepec Huntmaster are reachable by the creature tutors; Urza's Incubator only by Enlightened Tutor.

The second use is the reveal. 28 of the 99 are Dinosaur creature cards, so a seven-damage hit shows about two. Worldly Tutor and Congregation at Dawn cast after your draw step decide what the first cards are.

The third is Natural Order, which skips the climb: off a mana creature it puts Vaultborn Tyrant, Carnage Tyrant or a Ghalta onto the battlefield as early as turn three. Any green creature pays for it; the cheap ones to give up are the six mana creatures, Selvala, Huatli and Knight of the Stampede, and green tokens (Palani's Hatcher's Eggs, Regisaur Alpha's 3/3, the saga's 3/3s). Its targets must be green: Temple Altisaur, Wrathful Raptors, Trumpeting Carnosaur, Etali, Bonehoard Dracosaur, Bronzebeak Foragers and Kinjalli's Sunwing are out of its reach.

tutors.notes: The card goes on top, so cast in your main phase it is a turn of warning. Cast it at the end step before your turn to draw it, or in your own combat to aim the reveal. Two more calls: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds when the climb has stalled with a big body already out, since she taps for X equal to your greatest power; and Thrashing Brontodon when a lock piece is the problem.

targets.scenario: End step before your third turn, one green source untapped. Your hand is lands and Dinosaurs at four and five mana, and nothing in hand or on the battlefield makes a Dinosaur cheaper.
targets.why: Buy the discount. Knight takes {2} off every Dinosaur spell you cast, Gishath from the command zone included, and Otepec Huntmaster and Urza's Incubator stack on top of it. The cost reducer group is drawn by turn six in 52.5% of games, mean turn 3.827; this tutor is the second copy of it.

citations.quote: essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck

targets.scenario: Gishath is attacking and unblocked, blockers have been declared, and you hold {G}. Your draw step and Bonehoard Dracosaur's upkeep exile are behind you.
targets.why: Aim the reveal. The tutored card is the first of the cards he reveals, so one of the roughly two expected Dinosaurs is now a chosen one. Dreadmaw counts every other Dinosaur you control on resolution, Gishath and anything that entered with it included. Cast it before your draw step and you draw it instead, which is the other wish. Whether a reveal of this list's cards resolves the way stack 001's did needs a stack scenario.

citations.quote: First, the active player draws a card.

targets.scenario: Blasphemous Act is in your hand. Two seats have gone wide, a dozen creatures across the table, and your board is three Dinosaurs and two mana creatures.
targets.why: The Act cannot be tutored, so fetch the half that can. With the Altisaur out your other Dinosaurs take 1 each from the Act and live. The Act still kills every non-Dinosaur creature you control, both mana creatures here, so cast it when the table's board is worth more than your climb. Act and Altisaur are drawn together by turn six in 2.0% of games; on this list the line needs a stack scenario.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint

targets.scenario: Gishath is castable next turn. The seat you will attack holds mana up every turn and has flashed in a blocker twice this game.
targets.why: The wish nobody reads. Creatures your opponents control enter tapped, and a blocker must be untapped when it is declared, so whatever they flash in during your combat stands there. Three mana, a 2/3 flyer, and the lane is open the turn he swings.

tutors.notes: You choose the order, so choose it as a schedule. Cast at the end step before your turn, card one is this turn's draw and cards two and three are the next two. It says up to three; take two when a live draw is worth more than a known one. Cast in your combat after your draw step, all three are the top of Gishath's reveal.

targets.scenario: Gishath is attacking unblocked with Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Garruk's Uprising on the battlefield. Blockers have been declared and you hold {G}{G}{W}.
targets.why: Load the reveal. Stack three Dinosaurs: Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Vaultborn Tyrant and Regisaur Alpha. A hit of three or more puts all three onto the battlefield as one event: Uprising and Vaultborn each draw for every power-4 entry, Dreadmaw draws per other Dinosaur, Pantlaza discovers once, and Regisaur's token and haste are ready for next turn. Every count here is oracle text; the batch needs a stack scenario on this list.

citations.quote: First, the active player draws a card.

targets.scenario: A wrath has just resolved. You untap into seven lands and an empty board, Gishath is in the command zone with one recast behind him, and the table has turned on the seat that still has creatures.
targets.why: Rebuild through the payoff that needs no combat and no eight mana. Pantlaza discovers once a turn at the toughness of a Dinosaur that enters, so each body you cast from here is a body and a card. Take two: Pantlaza first, Vaultborn Tyrant second, and leave the third draw live. Gishath now costs {2} more.

targets.scenario: You are closing. Regisaur Alpha is on the battlefield with four other Dinosaurs, the seat to your left is at 14 with two small blockers, and it is the end step before your turn.
targets.why: Twelve trampling power for two mana. Ghalta costs {X} less where X is the total power of your creatures, and your board is already past ten. Regisaur Alpha gives other Dinosaurs haste, so she attacks the turn you draw her.

citations.quote: count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: One seat has a stax artifact out, another an enchantment that taxes your attacks, and a third a commander you cannot block. It is the end step before your turn and you have five mana next turn.
targets.why: The answer package. Stack Bronzebeak Foragers, then Thrashing Brontodon, then Tranquil Frillback. Foragers exiles up to one nonland permanent from each opponent when it enters, until it leaves; Brontodon sits on the battlefield as a {1} instant-speed answer to an artifact or enchantment; Frillback destroys one more on entry. Every answer to a lock piece in this deck is a creature, so this is how you get three.

citations.quote: Name your outs early

tutors.notes: Your only wish for a noncreature permanent, and it reaches seven: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Urza's Incubator, Roaming Throne, Mirari's Wake, Garruk's Uprising and Berserkers' Onslaught. None is a Dinosaur creature card, so never leave one on top for the reveal: it only spends a revealed slot. Cast it at the end step before your turn. Mirari's Wake is the call when a creature wipe has taken the dorks and you have seven lands: one extra mana per land, and it survives the next wipe.

targets.scenario: End step before your third turn, one white source untapped. Your hand is Dinosaurs at four and five mana and no cost reducer has shown.
targets.why: Fix the whole hand. Name Dinosaur and every Dinosaur creature spell costs {2} less, Gishath included. It is the one reducer the creature tutors cannot reach, and an artifact survives the sweeper that kills Knight of the Stampede and Otepec Huntmaster.

citations.quote: essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck

targets.scenario: Your hand is empty after a long game. You control a 6/6 and lands, and the next three draws are what you have.
targets.why: Turn the next bodies into cards. It draws on entry if you control a creature with power 4 or more, gives your creatures trample, and draws again for each power-4 creature that enters, revealed ones included. An enchantment survives a creature wipe.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint

targets.scenario: Gishath is on the battlefield and has dealt 7 commander damage to the seat with the board that beats yours. Next turn you have five mana and he can attack.
targets.why: Close with commander damage. Attacking creatures you control have double strike, so an unblocked Gishath deals 7 in each of two damage steps: 14 more, 21 in all. Whether he also reveals twice, and whether first-step arrivals change the second hit, needs a stack scenario. Keep a protection instant up for the swing.

targets.scenario: Vaultborn Tyrant and Earthshaker Dreadmaw are in hand, Gishath is on the battlefield, and you have four mana to spare this turn.
targets.why: The wish nobody sees. Name Dinosaur, and a triggered ability of another Dinosaur you control triggers an additional time: Vaultborn's draw and life, Dreadmaw's draw, Trumpeting Carnosaur's discover. A 4/4 with ward {2} that survives your own Act under Temple Altisaur. The extra trigger on Gishath's reveal and on Pantlaza's once-a-turn discover needs a stack scenario.

citations.quote: essentially an additional copy of any card in our deck

tutors.notes: A sorcery: it never answers removal on the stack. Tap the mana creature for mana first, then sacrifice it as the cost. Zacama, Primal Calamity arrives without its land untap, because that ability checks 'if you cast it' and a put is not a cast. The creature it finds still has every 'when this enters' trigger.

targets.scenario: Turn three. Three lands, Drover of the Mighty on the battlefield since turn two, Natural Order in hand, no Dinosaur in hand worth casting.
targets.why: The default. It enters, draws a card and gains 3 off its own trigger, and when it dies it leaves a token copy behind, so the first answer does not end it. A 6/6 trampler on turn three is a clock no seat has planned for.

citations.quote: Mana abilities must be activated before costs are paid.
The player pays the total cost.

targets.scenario: The blue seat holds counter mana every turn and the black seat has spent two spot removal spells on your Dinosaurs. Bloom Tender is on the battlefield.
targets.why: Fetch what they cannot point at. Natural Order itself can be countered, but once it resolves Carnage Tyrant is a hexproof 7/6 trampler, and a sweeper is the only way left. The Order is a sorcery, so cast it on a turn the counter seat tapped low on their own.

citations.quote: count the table's open mana before committing

targets.scenario: You are closing. Regisaur Alpha is on the battlefield, the seat to your left is at 12 with two chump blockers, and Faeburrow Elder is on the battlefield untapped.
targets.why: Twelve trampling power with haste. Regisaur Alpha gives other Dinosaurs haste and Ghalta is an Elder Dinosaur, so she attacks this turn, and trample carries everything past the blockers' toughness. Tap the Elder for mana, then sacrifice it to the Order: four mana, whatever your board looks like.

targets.scenario: Palani's Hatcher is on the battlefield with an Egg left. One seat has a lock enchantment and another a growing artifact board, and no mana creature is out.
targets.why: The cost nobody sees: an Egg is a 0/1 green Dinosaur creature token, so it pays for the Order. Zacama arrives as a 9/9 trampler with {2}{G} to destroy an artifact or enchantment and {2}{R} for 3 to a creature, every turn. No land untap, since it was put, not cast.

citations.quote: The ability triggers only if it is; otherwise it does nothing.

tutors.card: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People
tutors.notes: Two searches. On entry she finds a basic land: 7 Forest, 2 Mountain and 1 Plains in the 99. Flipped for {3}{R/W}{R/W} at sorcery speed she becomes a saga: two 3/3 Dinosaurs, then your creatures tap for {R}, {G} or {W}, then any Dinosaur card to hand, then double strike and trample for your Dinosaurs. Chapter three comes two turns after the flip.

targets.scenario: Huatli enters on turn three off green mana. Your lands make green and white, no red source is out, and Otepec Huntmaster is in hand.
targets.why: Fetch the colour most often missing. Red reads 0.548 on curve from lands alone and 0.694 with rocks and dorks, the lowest of the three. Otepec Huntmaster and Itzquinth want red on turn two or three.

targets.why: Ghalta costs {X} less for your creatures' total power and your creatures now tap for mana, so she is cast the turn you find her. Next turn chapter four gives your Dinosaurs double strike and trample: an unblocked 12/12 deals 24.

targets.scenario: Chapter three triggers. A seat has a creature that wins the game if it attacks next turn, and you will have six mana.
targets.why: The wish that is also removal. From hand, {2}{R} and a discard deal 3 to a creature or planeswalker at instant speed; cast instead, it is a 7/6 trampler that discovers 5. Hold it, and you choose which it is once you see their turn.

citations.quote: held answers rot

gaps: No tutor finds an instant or a sorcery. Blasphemous Act, Overwhelming Stampede, Rydia's Return and all five protection spells (Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Eerie Interlude, Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention) are unreachable. Hold the Act and fetch Temple Altisaur, never the reverse.

Every passing stack in this deck names at least one card v1.2.0 no longer runs, so no wish above rests on a verified line for this list. Needs a stack scenario: a Congregation-loaded reveal drawn only from this 99 (Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Vaultborn Tyrant, Regisaur Alpha with Pantlaza and Uprising out); Roaming Throne's extra trigger on Gishath and on Pantlaza; Berserkers' Onslaught as two reveals; Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur and Wrathful Raptors on this list's board; Natural Order into Vaultborn Tyrant.

Natural Order's targets must be green. Ten creatures in the 99 are not: Bonehoard Dracosaur, Bronzebeak Foragers, Etali, Hunting Velociraptor, Kinjalli's Sunwing, Otepec Huntmaster, Roaming Throne, Temple Altisaur, Trumpeting Carnosaur, Wrathful Raptors.

Read the unassisted goldfish figure for the Act-plus-Altisaur row (2.0% by turn six). Only the Altisaur half is tutorable; this guide has not checked whether the assisted figure (3.8%) credits a tutor for the Act half.

Three tutors deliver to the top of the library, so against a seat holding sweeper or discard mana the card can die in transit. Cast the instants at the end step before your turn to cut that exposure to your draw step. Forge has not seen v1.2.0, so no wish here has been watched in a game.
